name: Mirach
description: A star 61 parsecs away, 86 times the Sun's width, measured from its light.

radius.source: McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 5447: radius 86.471 solar radii, implied by the fitted luminosity 1403.71 solar luminosities (fractional uncertainty 0.074) and temperature

temperature.source: McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 5447: effective temperature 3802 +/- 125 K, from the fit of a model atmosphere to the star's spectral energy distribution (goodness of fit Q 0.048)

gravity.source: SIMBAD's compilation of spectroscopic measurements (mesFe_h): log g 1.05 from 2020AJ....160..120J; the 11 published values span log g 1 to 1.6, across which the limb law changes by at most 0.2% of the centre brightness

radialVelocity.source: Anderson & Francis (2012), Astronomy Letters 38, 331 (XHIP), Hipparcos astrometry, HIP 5447: RV 0.06 +/- 0.13 km/s (quality A)

distance.source: McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 5447: distance 60.533 pc, the paper's parallax inverted (Gaia DR1's where it revised the star's, else the Hipparcos reduction of van Leeuwen 2007; section 2.3; fractional uncertainty 0.034), at which the luminosity and radius hold

position.credit: Anderson & Francis (2012), Astronomy Letters 38, 331 (XHIP), Hipparcos astrometry

text.card: A star 61 parsecs away, 86 times the Sun's width, measured from its light.
text.introduction: Its brightness, measured band by band, gives 1,404 times the Sun's luminosity at 3,802 K, so 86.471 solar radii.
text.locator: Table 2, HIP 5447: D, Teff, L, Rad, Q

quotes.title: Mirach
quotes.card: It is pronounced and has the Bayer designation Beta Andromedae, which is Latinized from β Andromedae.
quotes.introduction: This star is positioned northeast of the Great Square of Pegasus and is potentially visible to all observers north of latitude 54° S. It is commonly used by stargazers to find the Andromeda Galaxy.
